title: Hindalco posts record quarterly profit of Rs 7,533 crore as copper and aluminium earnings jump
dek: The Aditya Birla metals company's September-quarter profit rose 59% on revenue of Rs 91,708 crore; its US arm Novelis recovered, but debt has risen as it builds new plants.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Hindalco Industries, the Aditya Birla group's aluminium and copper company, reported the highest quarterly profit and revenue in its history on Friday, helped by higher metal prices, a record quarter for its copper business and a recovery at its American subsidiary, Novelis.

Consolidated net profit for the July-September quarter rose 59% to Rs 7,533 crore from Rs 4,741 crore a year earlier, according to the company's results statement as reported. Revenue from operations rose 39% to Rs 91,708 crore, and earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rose 42% to Rs 13,757 crore. "Hindalco delivered its strongest-ever quarterly performance, with Revenue and PAT surpassing their previous highs," said Satish Pai, the managing director.

## Where the money came from

The Indian businesses did most of the work. EBITDA from the upstream aluminium business, which mines bauxite and smelts the metal, rose 55% to Rs 7,009 crore. The copper business, which includes a smelter at Dahej in Gujarat, reported record EBITDA of Rs 1,673 crore, up 164%. The aluminium and copper downstream businesses, which make products such as foil, extrusions and wire, also had a record quarter, the company said, without giving separate figures.

Hindalco has been trying to reduce its dependence on the London Metal Exchange (LME) price of aluminium, which it does not control. Its businesses not linked to LME prices generated Rs 6,860 crore of EBITDA, up 50%, about half of its total, the company said.

## Novelis recovers, but debt rises

Novelis, the Atlanta-based maker of rolled aluminium for drinks cans, cars and aircraft, had reported its own results a day earlier. Its net sales rose 25% to $5.9 billion, mainly because of higher aluminium prices, even though shipments of rolled products fell 2% to 919,000 tonnes. Adjusted EBITDA rose 20% to $508 million, or $553 a tonne, and net income rose 29% to $210 million, according to reports of the subsidiary's results.

Production at its plant in Oswego, New York, where a fire last year disrupted supply, is back to normal, and insurance payments for the fire have reached $519 million, the reports said. Its new plant at Bay Minette in Alabama produced its first coil from its cold rolling mill in September and is still being commissioned.

The cost of those projects shows up in the balance sheet. Novelis used $418 million of cash in its operations in the first half of the financial year, and Hindalco's consolidated net debt rose to 1.80 times EBITDA at the end of September, from 1.23 times a year earlier. The company said its new alumina refinery, aluminium smelter, copper smelter and coal mine projects in India were on schedule.

Hindalco's shares had fallen 3.1% to Rs 908.55 in early trade on Friday, before the results were announced.

## Other results on Friday

Several other companies reported September-quarter results on Friday, according to their filings as reported:

- Bosch: net profit up 18.7% to Rs 840.5 crore, revenue up 28% to Rs 7,655.1 crore; the board approved splitting each Rs 10 share into five Rs 2 shares, followed by a bonus issue of three shares for every one held
- Great Eastern Shipping: net profit more than doubled to Rs 1,269.23 crore; an interim dividend of Rs 14.40 a share, with 13 November as the record date
- Voltas: net profit up 53.5% to Rs 52.64 crore on revenue up 15.3% to Rs 2,707 crore
- Gland Pharma: net profit up 58% to Rs 291 crore

## What happens next

Indian markets reopen on Monday, when investors will react to the results. Analysts will also be watching aluminium and copper prices, and whether Novelis's new US plant starts contributing to earnings as planned.
